text:
jess_sales: FYI customer GigaHealth is ready to spin up their evaluation. They want a Private deployment in their lab next Tue. Can we run a quick prereq + access checklist in this thread?
ankit_se: 👍 yes. High-level: confirm GPU drivers/CUDA, container runtime, k8s version, network egress for registry, and how we'll hand them API/installer creds.
tina_eng: I'll paste the checklist we use for air-gapped-friendly installs. Short version: OS, drivers, container runtime, cgroup, device plugin, kubelet config, and storage.
fieldops_mark: On the hardware side they have A100 80GB and some T4s. Need to confirm MIG config and multi-GPU scheduling. Also want MIG enabled?
ankit_se: For A100s: MIG is optional but we support it. If they plan to use MIG we need nvidia-driver >= 470? (actually recommend >= 525 for CUDA12 compatibility). Recommend driver >=525 and CUDA 12.x runtime.
security_pep: Reminder: customer requires HSM/KMS integration and no outbound traffic except to our collector endpoints. Will they be fine with a short-lived outbound during install?
jess_sales: Customer prefers pull-through mirror for images. They can allow outbound only to our artifactory hostname for the installer (we can provide IPs).
tina_eng: OK. Minimal firewall openings for installer: outbound HTTPS to registry.redwood-inference.com (443), inbound SSH to bastion (we use a jumpbox), and kep ports to kube-api. For private mode the control plane talks to the private control plane via a single mTLS tunnel — that needs egress to our controlplane endpoint (we can use a customer-provided proxy).
ankit_se: Concrete prereq commands to run on each node (paste these to the customer):
```
# check GPU driver
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv
# check kernel and cgroup
uname -r; stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup
# container runtime
containerd --version || docker --version
# kubelet
kubectl version --short
```
fieldops_mark: Sample outputs we expect (they can paste back):
```
495.29.05, NVIDIA A100
Linux 5.15.0-101; cgroup2fs
containerd github.com/containerd/containerd 1.6.x
Client Version: v1.25.3
```
ankit_se: Notes: we prefer containerd (>=1.5) on Ubuntu 22.04. If they use Docker, ensure nvidia-docker2 or the nvidia-container-toolkit is present. cgroup v2 is preferred; if using cgroup v1 we need to enable legacy cgroups support in the installer.
security_pep: For KMS: we need KMS endpoint + audit logs. Also need confirmation that SSO is enforced for admin accounts.
jess_sales: For POC access we usually create a scoped API key (org:gigahealth-eval) that expires after 7d and a single install token for the private control plane. Is that acceptable?
fieldops_mark: Yes — we will also need a service account with cluster-admin on the install namespace only (we run the installer with that SA). Provide kubeconfig via secure upload to our SFTP or via the jumpbox.
tina_eng: Edge cases: if nodes are air-gapped we can push an offline bundle (tar+installer). They must provide a registry mirror URL and versioned manifests.
ankit_se: Device plugin details: deploy NVIDIA device plugin DaemonSet (we recommend nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:v0.11.0 or later) and nvidia-container-toolkit for runtime. Also enable GPU memory locking in kubelet: --feature-gates=DevicePlugins=true and resourceManager configs.
deploy-bot: Installer ticket created: REDWOOD-INTL-4521. Attach kubeconfig and logs to that ticket.
fieldops_mark: Quick checklist to confirm back to us before we schedule remote install (one-liner answers ok):
- OS & version (e.g., Ubuntu 22.04)
- Kernel version
- NVIDIA driver version
- CUDA runtime installed or we should use container images
- container runtime (containerd/docker) + version
- kube version and control plane reachable
- Pull-through registry or allowed egress to registry.redwood-inference.com
- KMS/HSM details and requirements
- Admin contact and jumpbox SSH (IP)

security_pep: Also include: list of sensitive namespaces/pods that must be excluded from logs, and retention period for audit logs.
jess_sales: I'll send the customer the commands + checklist and ask for answers by EOD tomorrow. If they pass we can book a 90-min install window next Tue.
ankit_se: If they fail a driver check we can help upgrade in-session, but they'll need sudo and reboot window.
fieldops_mark: One more: if the customer uses SELinux enforce or custom kernels we should run a compatibility test — let us know early.
jess_sales: Thanks team — I'll follow up with customer now and paste their reply here. :rocket:
